# gerrit-stack efficiency benchmark

*Generated by `evals/metrics/collect.py` on 2026-10-18 16:48 UTC.*

Does the plugin make an agent produce Gerrit relation chains that are cut by concern, correct, and cheaper to get to review than the same agent without it, and does it keep a chain intact through rework and review? Four arms on identical tasks: A–C from pass 2, D added on 2026-10-18.

> **Pass 2 (2026-10-05): 4 suites × 3 arms × 3 runs = 90 runs, 0 errors, $92.53; every run passed the
> startup isolation check on `claude-opus-5-5`.** Rules in force: concern is the unit, size is a soft
> warning (400 production lines), no chain-depth cap, split granularity is the author's call (rubrics do
> not judge it), commits linted at 72 columns, team files in every arm's fixture. Rework and reviewer
> suites ran before the granularity change (neither depends on it) and were re-graded with the tightened
> Change-Id check (`evals/metrics/regrade.py`, one false positive flipped). Concern-map purity is
> informational only. Forged or hand-typed Change-Ids show as failures of the `no-manual-change-id`
> grader, not in the Guardrails table. 3 runs per cell: read differences of one or two runs as noise.

> **Arm D (2026-10-18): the gerrit-stack port in the official plugin, 4 suites × 3 runs = 30 runs, 0
> errors, $30.11; every run passed the isolation check on `claude-opus-5-5`. A–C are pass 2, not re-run.**
> D loads the official plugin from a `gerrit-mcp-server` checkout, 9 commits on origin/master (head
> `55ec2e1`): chain rules in `gerrit-workflow`, `stack-planner`, `gerrit-review`, a PreToolUse git guard,
> conventions read from the repo's docs, and a SessionStart context in Gerrit repos. No gerrit-stack plugin.
>
> | | D upstream | C gerrit-stack | B mcp-only | A vanilla |
> |---|---|---|---|---|
> | S1 unprompted, runs passed | 12/12 | 10/12 | 7/12 | 9/12 |
> | S2 prompted split, runs passed | 9/9 | 8/9 | 9/9 | 7/9 |
> | S3 seeded-chain rework, runs passed | 5/6 | 6/6 | 1/6 | 4/6 |
> | S4 review, runs passed | 2/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 |
> | Runs with a forged or re-typed Change-Id (all suites) | 1 | 0 | 6 | 3 |
> | Nudged runs that used `--no-verify` (S1 + S3) | 0/9 | 0/9 | 6/9 | 6/9 |
> | Review comments in the team's format | 16/16 | 19/19 | 0/16 | 6/18 |
>
> Read D against C as "the port keeps what C measured", within noise. D's caveats are under "Open after
> arm D" below. Reproduce D: `python3 evals/run.py --arms upstream --runs 3 -j 3 --push-to
> http://localhost:8080/a/demo-plugin --eval-dir evals/bench-<suite>` (S1 adds `--case maintenance-mode
> --case rate-limited-ping --variants natural,nudged`, S3 adds `--variants natural,nudged`); the
> checkout defaults to `~/workspace/open/gerrit-mcp-server` (`--upstream-plugin-dir`).

## Open after arm D

1. **A re-typed Change-Id still gets through on amend.** One nudged rework run wrote the commit's own
   Change-Id into a heredoc message file and ran `git commit --amend -F`. The value was right, so the
   change kept its patch sets, but one typo would have opened a new change instead. The upstream guard
   accepts any Change-Id on `--amend -F` by design (re-applying the one Gerrit shows must keep working),
   and the skill's recipe (`git log -1 --format=%B > <file>`, edit, `--amend -F`) was not used. Options:
   deny a Change-Id typed on `--amend` that differs from HEAD's, or deny any trailer composed in the same
   command and name the recipe. C had no such run.
2. **D's unprompted chains are coarser; the cause is a newer planner rule, not the port.** D folds the
   ~40-line "add the setting" change into the change that first reads it: rate-limited-ping is 2 changes
   in every D run against 3–4 in 17 of 18 A–C runs, and maintenance-mode opens with a 404–569-line
   change in every D run where half of the A–C runs (9 of 18) open with a ~32-line config change. Both planners gained "no class without a caller" on
   2026-10-18, after pass 2. Single concern, builds alone and one Change-Id per change match C (100 %). Comparing chain length with C fairly needs C re-run on S1 with the current planner (≈ $16).
3. **Labelled review replies differ by fixture wording.** In rework, D labelled 3 of 6 replies, C 0 of 5.
   D's `AGENTS.md` says "label every review comment"; gerrit-stack's `comment-style = conventional`
   labels new comments and leaves replies free-form. Align the `AGENTS.md` wording before quoting that
   row.
4. **Review suite: D 2/3 against C 3/3, same defects found (5/9), every comment labelled.** The failing
   run's judge objected to a vote mentioned in the summary text; no vote was posted. D has no
   reviewer-side skill: its labels come from `AGENTS.md` alone.
5. **Comparability.** D ran 13 days after A–C, on Claude Code 2.1.302 (A–C: 2.1.289), with an
   `AGENTS.md` A–C lack (committed in S1/S2; untracked in S3/S4, because the seed push drops the
   fixture's base commit). Qualification limits the version concern: C re-run on the 7 eval cases with
   the current CLI scored 6/7 and 0.964, the same as D.
6. **Upstream state and a gap the benchmark could not see.** The 9 commits are local, not pushed. The
   guard and the session context run from the plugin's environment and stay silent while it lacks their
   console scripts. After an update, the first session can run without them, and `check-config` does
   not say so. The runner rebuilt that environment and probed both hooks before every D batch, so no D
   run was affected.
7. **One eval grader fails C and D alike.** `split-over-budget`'s `planner-invoked` expects
   `stack-planner`; both arms planned through their main skill (`gerrit-stack`, `gerrit-workflow`) and
   still split by concern. Accept the main skill there, or keep the grader as a strict check.

## Arms

Same prompts, same fixture repos, same pinned model, four arms in a scrubbed sandbox (environment allowlist, account connectors off, startup check against a per-arm allowlist):

- **A — `without`**: vanilla Claude Code, no plugins (the floor).
- **B — `mcp-only`**: vanilla + the official `gerrit@gerrit-mcp` plugin (its MCP server and `gerrit-workflow` skill).
- **C — `with`**: B + `gerrit-stack` (this plugin) honouring the team files. **C vs B is the honest claim**; C vs A shows the floor.
- **D — `upstream`**: the official plugin loaded from a `gerrit-mcp-server` checkout that carries the gerrit-stack skills and guard ported upstream (`gerrit-workflow` chain rules, `stack-planner`, `gerrit-review`, a PreToolUse git guard), without `gerrit-stack`. Its fixtures add an `AGENTS.md` stating the team conventions, because the ported skills read conventions from the repository's docs rather than from `.gerrit-stack`. **D vs C asks whether the port keeps what C measured.** D ran later than A–C (see Sources for the Claude Code version and the checkout).

Outcome metrics come from `scripts/chain-metrics.sh --json` over each run's workspace; process/cost metrics from the stream-json trace (`type: result` → cost, turns, duration) and the hook trace (`GERRIT_STACK_TRACE`: `ask`/`deny` per verb). Cells are `mean / median` over runs, rates are `share (count/total)`; deltas are differences of means (percentage points for rates).

## Reading the numbers

- **1 run per cell shows the shape** of the behaviour (did it split, did the fix land on the right change, was anything posted); **3 runs per cell** are needed before reading differences between arms as numbers.
- **Seeded chain = identical starting point**: in the rework and reviewer scenarios every arm starts from the same hand-written chain pushed by the runner, so differences come from the session, not from what an earlier session happened to produce.
- **Team files are present in every arm's fixture** (`.gerrit-stack`, the commitlint config): they belong to the repo. Arms A and B simply have no tooling that honours them.
- **Errored runs** (session crashed, or the sandbox startup check found something unexpected) are excluded from the means; they are always counted under Isolation and in each section's `Runs / errors` line.
- Paths that belong to no concern of a case's concern map do not count for purity or completeness.
- **Size is information, not a target.** *Production lines* are insertions + deletions outside tests, docs and lock/generated files; the tables show their median and the largest change, plus the chain's test lines. No row passes or fails on size; `–` means the run predates these counts.

## Split quality

Deterministic measures of how well a chain is cut, per suite and case (natural variant). *Purity*: share of changes that carry exactly one concern of the case's concern map; *completeness*: share of concerns that live in exactly one change; *builds alone*: share of changes on which the fixture's verify command passes when checked out alone; *tests travel*: share of changes touching `src/main` Java code that also touch a test. Production and test lines are shown for information only (no pass/fail).

## Rework (seeded chain)

The runner pushes the fixture's hand-written chain, reviewer `rena` posts `Code-Review -1` with one blocking thread on a change in the middle, one agent session reworks the chain, the runner pushes again and reads Gerrit back. Every arm starts from the same chain. The nudged variant adds one plausible bad instruction.

## Reproduce

```
make demo-up demo-seed      # local Gerrit for the pushes
python3 evals/run.py --eval-dir evals/bench-unprompted --arms with,mcp-only,without --runs 1
python3 evals/run.py --eval-dir evals/bench-split      --arms with,mcp-only,without --runs 1
python3 evals/run.py --eval-dir evals/bench-rework     --arms with,mcp-only,without --runs 1 \
    --variants natural,nudged --push-to <gerrit-project-url>
python3 evals/run.py --eval-dir evals/bench-review     --arms with,mcp-only,without --runs 1 \
    --push-to <gerrit-project-url>
python3 evals/metrics/collect.py --out docs/benchmark.md   # add --json PATH for the raw report
```

Each runner call writes `evals/results/<timestamp>/{aggregate-result.json,runs/<case>[@<variant>]/<arm>/<n>/…}`; `collect.py` renders this page from every results directory it finds (or the ones passed with `--results`). Use `--runs 3` for numbers. Targets: exactly-one-Change-Id 100 %, rule violations 0, cost overhead ≤ +30 % vs arm B. Change size is reported, never a target.
